Date: 2026-06-10T09:15:00Z
Subject: Kickoff: Cross-border MAP & EU data-localization review

Hi Sofia / Oliver —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. As promised, this thread will act as the mutual action plan (MAP) kickoff so we can align owners, milestones, and any EU data-residency constraints up front. Attached are two docs to get us started: a short MAP template and our EU data-localization overview.

Goal: 2-week evaluation & legal/technical review that leaves both sides ready to agree on scope and a production timeline (we should be able to present a recommended configuration by 2026-06-24).

Proposed owners (please confirm or reassign):
- Commercial / Program lead: Sofia Marin (Euratek)
- Procurement: procurement@euratek.com
- Security / DPO: Oliver Hansen (Euratek)
- Redwood technical lead: Markus Klein (markus_klein@redwood.ai) — infra & deployment options
- Redwood legal / compliance: Laura Bennett (laura_bennett@redwood.ai) — DPA/SLA/DPA redline owner
- Solutions / integration: Vivek Kulkarni (vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai) — implementation questions

Key items for this MAP kickoff:
1) Data residency constraints: confirm whether EU-only storage/processing is required for logs, KV cache, model telemetry, and backups.
2) Architecture options: Redwood Hosted (EU region), Dedicated (reserved capacity in customer VPC in eu-west-1), or Private (on-prem / air-gapped) — pros/cons and footprints.
3) Security evidence: SOC 2 report, DPA, encryption at rest / in transit notes.
4) Procurement items & timeline: initial SOW + pricing cadence and any required PO process.

Next steps: please confirm owners and availability for a 30–45 minute sync the week of 2026-06-15 — we propose Wednesday 2026-06-16 at 10:00 CEST (calendar placeholder attached).

Attachments: MAP-Euratek-Template.xlsx, EU-Data-Residency-Overview.pdf

If you prefer, we can split the MAP into a short legal track and a technical track with separate checkpoints — happy to adapt.

Thanks,

Hannah Schmitt

Subject: Re: Kickoff: Cross-border MAP & EU data-localization review

Thanks Hannah — appreciate the concise plan. A few quick clarifications before we lock in owners and the call: 

- EU-only requirement: Our board has asked that production customer data and backups remain physically in the EU. Can you confirm, at a technical level, what "Redwood Hosted (EU region)" entails re: backups and telemetry? Is there any cross-border fallback behavior?

- On-prem option: What is the minimum infra spec (GPU / storage) for a dedicated deployment for our expected 50 rps peak? We may need to involve our infra team.

- Compliance artifacts: Please send SOC 2 and your standard DPA template. We will circulate redlines from legal.

- Point of contact for technical deep-dive: do we have a single person to contact for implementation questions?

Happy to take the proposed Wednesday slot if others confirm.

Best,
Sofia Marin
Head of Product Integration
Euratek Ltd

Hi Sofia — great questions. Quick assignments from our side so you know who to ping: 

- Markus will be your infra contact for the Dedicated/Private options and sizing: markus_klein@redwood.ai.
- Laura will handle the DPA/SLA review and SOC 2: laura_bennett@redwood.ai. Expect the current SOC 2 summary and our DPA draft by end of day.
- Vivek will run a short implementation note that outlines the difference between Hosted-EU and Dedicated with respect to telemetry and backups; he'll include recommended config that meets EU-only storage.

Answering Sofia's first two bullets briefly: Hosted (EU region) keeps data in our eu-west-1 region for serving and storage; telemetry defaults to the same region but there are opt-outs we can enable for strict customers; backups can be configured to remain in-region (we'll provide the exact retention & encryption parameters). We will not require cross-border fallback unless explicitly allowed in the MAP fallback policy.

I'll attach a short infra note now (RD-Infrastructure-Notes.pdf) — it covers minimum GPU footprint estimates for your 50 rps baseline and also shows an option for burst capacity.

Marissa
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
